job.title: Head of CX & Marketing (Scale up brand)
job.description:
Head of Marketing and CX


Central London, hybrid (3 days a week in the office)


£85,000 to £105,000 plus 20% bonus


A growing UK business with plans to become a household name is hiring a Head of Marketing to lead marketing and communications through its next stage of growth.


The business is scaling quickly, opening new locations and growing its app and digital services. You will set the marketing strategy, the plan and the measures, and lead a team of 5 to deliver across consumer, business and corporate audiences.


What you will be responsible for


• Marketing strategy, the annual plan and the campaign calendar

• Awareness, acquisition and growth across digital and physical channels

• PR, external communications and employer brand

• Defining and embedding the customer value proposition

• Launch marketing for new locations and new digital features

• B2B marketing and growing partnership income

• KPIs and monthly reporting, so spend shows a clear return

• Leading a team of 5 and managing the agency partners


About you


This role is number 2 to a member of the executive team, with influence beyond your remit. You will bring:


• Senior marketing leadership, with ownership of strategy, budget, people and results

• A track record of growing a brand, ideally through a scale-up or challenger stage

• Structure and commercial focus. You talk in metrics, set a long-term plan and break it into yearly deliverables

• Strength in digital, CRM and social, plus PR and communications. Retail experience is welcome

• A knack for making a modest budget work hard, and for making the case for more

• The confidence to challenge, hold the line on the brand and deputise for your manager

• A visible leader who wants to be in the office with a growing London team

• A marketing qualification (CIM or equivalent) is preferred, or an MBA backed by a successful marketing career


The package


• £85,000 to £110,000 base salary

• 20% bonus

• 25 days holiday plus bank holidays, and your birthday off

• 5% employer pension

• 3 days a week in a central London office, on days you choose

• Flexible start and finish times (core 9-6)


The role needs regular presence in central London, so you will need to live within a reasonable commute.

job.title: Director of CX
job.description:
Director of Customer Experience

£100,000, permanent

App-led consumer brand, national retail estate

A UK consumer brand with a national estate of retail sites and a customer app at the centre of its growth is hiring a Director of Customer Experience. You'll report to the Chief Customer Officer and own how customers experience the brand across the app, the contact centre and the sites themselves.

The role

  • Lead around 75 people across customer experience, customer operations and the customer-facing sites.
  • Own the end-to-end experience: digital journeys, assisted service, complaints, Voice of the Customer and insight.
  • Hold the app commercially. Adoption, membership and repeat usage are yours to grow.
  • Run a 24/7 support operation in a regulated environment, with in-house and outsourced teams. Zendesk is in place and AI agent pilots are under way, so the next stage is yours to shape.
  • Hold the P&L for a customer-facing retail estate of around £8m revenue.
  • Deputise for the CCO across customer, marketing, operations and revenue.

About you

  • You've led customer experience at Head of or Director level in a consumer business where digital and physical service meet, such as retail, travel, energy or mobility.
  • You use contact and complaint data to fix causes upstream, and you can show the numbers that moved.
  • You've owned a P&L and built a proposition or membership product.
  • You've delivered change through peers in product, technology and finance.

What's on offer

  • 100k base salary
  • Ownership of growth, transformation, contact centre and CX strategy
  • London based 1-2 times per week
  • Opportunities to represent the business through various events and partnerhsips

job.title: Customer Journey Consultant
job.description:
Interim CX Consultant: Customer Journey Redesign

Yorkshire, 3 days per week on site | Start late October 2026 | Day rate on experience

A privately owned business has grown quickly, and its customer journey has grown piece by piece alongside it. They now want it mapped as one journey and rebuilt.

The assignment

  • Map the current journey end to end, across every route a customer arrives by.
  • Design the future journey, moving the team towards proactive contact.
  • Find the friction and the duplicated steps, and remove tasks that no longer need doing.
  • Write the process maps and procedures that sit behind the new journey, with metrics underneath.
  • Work side by side with a CRM developer joining the business, so the new workflows are built as you design them.

How you will work

You will sit with the customer care team, watch how the work is done and write it up yourself. Your first 2 weeks produce the current picture and a roadmap, with the quick wins first. The business wants to move fast, so pace counts.

About you

  • You have taken a customer journey from first map to launch and can show what changed.
  • You look at the journey as a whole and question whether each step needs to exist.
  • You are comfortable in a growing business without big project teams around you.
  • Experience in a regulated sector is useful.

job.title: Customer Success Manager
job.description:
Customer Success Manager | SaaS, Contact Centre Platform


About the business

A fast-growing technology provider whose platform helps a large number of businesses connect with their customers every day. The culture is ambitious and down to earth. You are trusted with responsibility early, expected to think commercially and encouraged to act decisively. It is also a supportive place to do that: people are open and honest, and mistakes are treated as part of learning quickly.


The role

This is a senior, customer-facing role leading new implementation projects from first discovery through to go-live. You sit between what a customer needs and what the platform can deliver, and you design solutions that show value from day one.

You work directly with customers to understand their business pains and map them to platform features. You then produce a solution design for the System Build team to configure. Once it is built, you own testing and quality assurance before handing back to the customer for go-live. You own the design and everything about its quality, but you do not configure it yourself.

What you will do

  • Discovery and solution design
  • Lead structured discovery sessions to surface business pains, objectives and success criteria
  • Map requirements to platform capabilities, making full use of the customer's contracted package
  • Produce clear designs covering call flows, routing logic, IVR frameworks, integrations and reporting, ready for handoff
  • Challenge customers constructively where their first idea would limit outcomes or cause problems later
  • Spot opportunities to widen adoption beyond the minimum scope

Project delivery

  • Own the project plan from kick-off to go-live, delivering to agreed dates and within estimated resource hours
  • Coordinate handoffs between discovery, build, testing and go-live
  • Manage scope, timeline and risk, flagging early and resolving before problems grow
  • Close every project with a full handover to Customer Success, including documented outcomes and a feature adoption baseline
  • Testing and go-live
  • Validate that the configured solution matches the approved design and meets the customer's success criteria
  • Manage sign-off, live support during launch and resolution of critical issues
  • Leave customers self-sufficient, with knowledge transfer and documentation complete
  • Value, adoption and commercial awareness
  • Drive feature adoption throughout implementation, with customers using a strong majority of the features in their package at go-live
  • Define and document success outcomes before go-live so the Customer Success Manager has a clear baseline
  • Pass on upsell and expansion opportunities to the account team
  • Contribute to monthly professional services fee targets across your projects and spot additional work where customer needs grow


About you

Essential

  • A few years in customer-facing implementation, solutions consulting or technical onboarding in a SaaS environment
  • Experience with contact centre platforms
  • A track record of delivering complex SaaS implementations on time and within scope
  • Strong discovery and consultative skills, with the ability to turn real business needs into effective designs
  • Disciplined project management and comfort owning a delivery plan
  • Clear communication with everyone from operational managers to IT leads
  • Commercial awareness of how adoption, outcomes and retention connect

Helpful to have

  • Experience designing contact centre solutions (routing, IVR, workforce management, CRM integrations)
  • CRM integration familiarity
  • Time spent in or alongside a Customer Success function
  • Understanding of AI-driven contact centre capabilities such as conversation analytics, AI routing and virtual agents

Training and progression

Full platform certification, implementation methodology and discovery framework training, exposure to a wide range of enterprise contact centre environments, ongoing development as the platform's AI capabilities grow, and clear progression within Customer Success and Professional Services.


Benefits

  • 25 days annual leave plus your birthday off, increasing with length of service
  • Buy and sell holiday options
  • Enhanced maternity and paternity packages
  • Life insurance
  • Enhanced pension options
  • Company-paid sick leave
  • Personal training allowance
  • Social, charity and culture committee events

job.title: Head of Customer Insight
job.description:
Customer Insight Lead


Social housing | Hybrid, Liverpool | £60,000


Turn data that is rich but siloed into something the whole business can make decisions on.


The organisation holds plenty of rich information on its service users: contact reasons, complaints, repairs history, satisfaction survey results, digital journeys. It sits in separate places and rarely gets used together. This role brings it into one picture and puts it in front of the people making decisions, across the customer function and the wider business.


What you'll do

  • Bring together what the organisation holds on service users across every channel, digital and otherwise, and turn it into evidence decision makers can use
  • Break down the gaps between data sources, so contact, complaints, repairs and survey data get read as one picture rather than several
  • Work across the customer function and the wider business: finance, operations, and the board, not just the team that owns customer experience
  • Sit on the new residents committee, bringing evidence into a forum where tenants have a direct say in the decisions that affect them
  • Keep pace with the regulatory environment shaping the sector and translate what it means for the numbers you own
  • Build the case for a decision on evidence rather than instinct, and hold that line in rooms where the instinct is strong


Our ideal applicant

  • Objective. You follow the data to its conclusion even when it is inconvenient
  • Commercially minded, able to connect service user data to decisions with a cost or a return attached, not only to satisfaction scores
  • Has broken down data silos before, and knows what it takes to get different systems and teams working from the same picture
  • Understands the regulatory pressures shaping social housing today, and what they mean operationally, not just for compliance reporting
  • Comfortable holding data from several sources at once: digital platforms, phone contact, home visits, complaints, surveys
  • An individual contributor by choice, confident presenting findings to people well outside the customer function, including residents themselves


The package

  • £60,000 base salary
  • Hybrid, based in Liverpool a few days a week
  • Benefits detail shared on application

﻿

All applications are handled confidentially by Stellify.

job.title: Customer Service & Insights Manager
job.description:
Customer Insight and Performance Manager


Liverpool (office based) | £40,000 to £44,000 including car allowance


Own performance, insight and regulatory compliance for a small, regulated property business where reporting goes all the way to Board. This role is the organisation's eyes: what's working, what's at risk, and what the data says should change.


The remit is broad for the size of business, and that's the appeal. You'll build the performance framework rather than inherit one, and your reporting will sit in front of Board and leadership every cycle.


What you'll own

  • The performance and insight framework: designing it, running it, and making it the way the business understands itself
  • Regulatory compliance and assurance: monitoring statutory and regulatory requirements, coordinating reporting for regulatory returns, internal reviews and external audits
  • Board reporting: papers, dashboards and exception reports that hold up to scrutiny
  • Customer complaints and feedback analysis, turned into recommendations that change how services run
  • Contractor and partner performance: KPIs, SLAs, and the meetings where accountability actually happens
  • Business systems and data improvement: better data quality, simpler workflows, and supporting new systems from testing through to training
  • Line management of a Compliance Officer, plus mentoring apprentices


Our ideal applicant

  • A customer-led performance leader: uses insight, complaints and service data to improve customers' experience, and can show where it worked
  • Strong on statutory and regulatory compliance, and confident being the person the organisation relies on to stay ahead of it
  • Skilled at data interrogation and analysis, and clearer still at explaining what the numbers mean to a Board
  • Comfortable challenging contractors and partners while keeping the relationship working


The package

  • £40,000 to £45,000, including car allowance
  • 35 hours, Monday to Friday, with flexi time
  • Office based in Liverpool
  • Pension with employer contribution
  • 25 days holiday plus bank holidays


All applications are handled confidentially by Stellify.
